data.title: SA analyst upgrades/downgrades: NVDA, MSFT, GOOG, SNDK
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) received an upgrade following CEO Jensen Huang's rapid reinstatement, while Alphabet (GOOG) saw its rating lifted after a significant price decline brought shares to technical support levels. On the downgrade side, Sandisk (SNDK) faces concerns about a potential NAND cycle peak and intensifying Chinese competition, while Microsoft (MSFT) drew a sell rating as analysts warn that rising depreciation from AI infrastructure spending will erode the company's historically strong margins.

Upgrades

  • Nvidia (NVDA): Upgrade to Buy by Ragmar Rikberg. The analyst cites Jensen Huang's return as CEO and attractive valuation at roughly 9x fiscal 2028 forward earnings as key reasons for the upgrade, noting that NVDA's full-stack strategy deepens ecosystem integration across AI factories, agents, and robotics.

"The ecosystem Jensen has built around Nvidia—and continues to build—is nothing short of exceptional...I think now, assuming Jensen remains at the helm, Nvidia's updated fiscal 2028 outlook, with growth expectations raised from 70% to 75%, provides a reasonable foundation for valuation assessment. In case those growth assumptions hold, Nvidia trades at roughly 9x fiscal 2028 forward earnings."

  • Alphabet (GOOG): Upgrade Sell to Hold by Damir Tokic. The analyst upgraded shares after the stock fell nearly 35% from its May highs, reaching technical support around $260, though fundamental concerns about AI disruption to Google Search and negative free cash flows remain.

"Alphabet is now almost 35% below its all-time highs reached in May—it lost more than a third of its value already. Technically, it reached the support on the 5Y chart right around $260. Thus, it makes sense to temporarily upgrade Alphabet to a Hold (Neutral)."

Downgrades

  • Sandisk (SNDK): Downgrade to Hold by Hunting Alphas. The analyst warns that NAND may be nearing a cyclical peak as Chinese cloud providers cut enterprise SSD orders and consumer demand weakens, while competition from Chinese chipmaker YMTC threatens to pressure global NAND pricing.

"The NAND memory segment is starting to face headwinds that suggest we may be closer to the cyclical peak. Chinese cloud service providers (CSPs) are cutting down their enterprise SSD orders, as they aren't monetizing AI demand as well to justify forking out higher-priced memory. ... I expect this to accelerate a downturn in the NAND cycle and structurally weaken the market shares position of players such as Sandisk."

  • Microsoft (MSFT): Downgrade Hold to Sell by Elina Selianska. The analyst argues that Microsoft's transformation from a zero-production-cost software business to cloud and AI infrastructure will permanently compress margins as depreciation from massive capital spending begins flowing through the income statement.

"Investors still value Microsoft by the standards of an old software giant with zero production cost, while the business is already transforming into infrastructure with an endless cycle of chip replacement and a margin sliding down. When such a restructuring of the business is layered on the tough policy of the Fed, geopolitics, and problems with government debt, holding the capitalization at $3.7 trillion on stubbornness alone won't work."

data.title: Faraday Future announces about $41M investment in FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem
data.description:
• Faraday Future Intelligent Electric (FFAI) announced on Friday an investment in FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem (FFR) worth around $41 million.
  • FFR said that it filed a preliminary Schedule 14C with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 25, marking the completion of all material matters required of both parties post deal closing.  
  • As of November 25, 2026, FFAI beneficially held roughly 14.7 million shares of FFR common stock, representing around 53% of outstanding common shares.
  • Following completion of the deal, FFAI would hold around 80.1 million common shares, representing about 75% of the resulting outstanding common stock of FFR.
  • All newly issued FFR shares received by FFAI in the transaction are subject to an 18-month lock-up period.
  • Press Release

data.title: Wall Street firmly in green as it looks to end volatile week on a high
data.description:
Wall Street rose on Friday as it hoped to close out a volatile week with a winning session, while Treasury yields moved higher following the Thanksgiving holiday break.

S&P 500 (SP500) +1.1%, the Dow (DJI) +1%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) +1.4%.

Wall Street returned to trading after the Thanksgiving holiday, with investors looking to end a turbulent week on a positive note. The market has experienced sharp swings, with significant gains followed by heavy selloffs.

On the economic front, investors will monitor the Federal Reserve's balance sheet report. U.S. stock markets will also close early on Friday for the Black Friday holiday session.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 4.2 basis points to 4.70%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 5.1 basis points to 4.92%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) rose 5.1 basis points to 5.30%.

Among S&P 500 stocks, Sandisk +11.48%, Lumentum +10.24%, Synchrony Financial +10.19%, Coherent +10.17%, and Bloom Energy +9.67%.

Essex Property Trust -24.75%, State Street -8.98%, Vertex Pharmaceuticals -7.38%, Federal Realty -5.00%, and Arch Capital -3.80%.

data.title: 30 large-cap stocks flashing Strong Buy rating
data.description:
As we draw close to the end of the year, several large cap stocks continue to earn top marks from Seeking Alpha’s Quant system.

The rankings point to strength across several sectors, although energy, financials, and technology-related stocks account for a significant share of the list. As of Nov. 27, the top 112 ranked stocks carry a Strong Buy Quant Rating, with scores ranging from 4.50 to 4.99.

Seeking Alpha’s Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions, and price momentum relative to their sector peers.

Energy stocks lead the rankings

Energy is the most prominent sector in the screen. Integrated oil and gas companies, refiners and exploration and production firms together account for a substantial number of the top-rated stocks.

Marathon Petroleum (MPC) ranks fourth overall with a 4.98 Quant score, followed by Valero Energy (VLO) at 4.98 and Phillips 66 (PSX) at 4.97. Chevron (CVX), Shell (SHEL), HF Sinclair (DINO), ConocoPhillips (COP), TotalEnergies (TTE), Repsol (REPYY), Eni (E), and Suncor Energy (SU) also feature among the top 30.

The broader list includes other energy names such as EOG Resources (EOG), Permian Resources (PR), Venture Global (VG), Cenovus Energy (CVE), Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ), and Diamondback Energy (FANG).

Semiconductors and technology hardware remain strong

Semiconductors and technology hardware are another major cluster. Micron Technology (MU) is ranked second overall with a 4.99 Quant score, while Dell Technologies (DELL) ranks third at 4.98.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Texas Instruments (TXN), and Sandisk (SNDK) also make the top 30. Further down the ranking, ASE Technology (ASX), Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM), Skyworks Solutions (SWKS), Marvell Technology (MRVL), Broadcom (AVGO), Western Digital (WDC), United Microelectronics (UMC), Synopsys (SNPS) and Seagate Technology (STX) carry Strong Buy ratings.

Software names also feature, including Unity Software (U), Rubrik (RBRK), Salesforce (CRM) and Workday (WDAY).

Financial stocks add to sector breadth

Financials are another significant contributor, with 12 banks and financial companies appearing in the top 112 with Strong Buy rating. These include Allstate (ALL), Equitable Holdings (EQH), Reinsurance Group of America (RGA), and Corpay (CPAY) among the top 30.

The broader screen also features Citigroup (C), Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD), Royal Bank of Canada (RY), Regions Financial (RF), Fifth Third Bancorp (FITB), Wells Fargo (WFC), UBS Group (UBS) and Bank of Montreal (BMO).

Healthcare names are represented by Moderna (MRNA), Centene (CNC), Roivant Sciences (ROIV) and BrightSpring Health Services (BTSG) in the top 30.

data.title: PetMed Express adopts tax benefit preservation plan to mitigate tax exposure during profitable years
data.description:
Shares of PetMed Express (PETS) are gaining ground into Friday’s open following the disclosure of a tax benefit preservation plan that will enable the company to use its prior losses to offset any future gains and mitigate its tax liability in those years.

The plan was adopted to prevent changes in stock ownership from eliminating any future tax benefits.

The company defines an “ownership change” that could impact the tax benefit as one in which the percentage of stock owned by any shareholder increases in the aggregate by more than 50 percentage points over the lowest percentage of stock owned by that shareholder over the prior three-year period or sooner.

While the plan cannot prevent anyone from acquiring a significant holding, it is intended to reduce the likelihood of such an event by deterring any person from acquiring beneficial ownership of 4.9% or more without the Board’s approval.

PetMed Express (PETS) has not earned a profit since the second quarter of 2025.

data.title: HubSpot downgraded by Argus amid worries about turnaround
data.description:
• HubSpot (HUBS) was downgraded by investment firm Argus on Friday amid worries about the marketing software company's turnaround.
  • Shares rose fractionally in premarket trading.
  • “We see HubSpot as a company in turnaround. HubSpot's management has been swept away, and cofounder Brian Halligan has returned to the CEO role,” Argus analyst Joseph Bonner wrote in a note to clients. “But can HubSpot find its place in the emerging agentic AI paradigm? HubSpot is an early-stage customer relationship management software company focused on small and midsize businesses that have traditionally been overlooked by larger CRM providers. The price sensitivity and increasing reluctance of customers to close new deals is impacting HubSpot. HUBS touts its broad platform of services as an advantage in a market where customers are looking to consolidate spending at a smaller number of vendors. Like many peers, it has restructured several times, laying off staff and consolidating real estate leases, which has supported margins. However, we may have to wait until 4Q results for new management to reveal its turnaround plans.”
  • Bonner lowered his rating on HubSpot to Hold from Buy and removed his price target.

data.title: SAP source code target of cyberattack; company says no customer data compromised: report
data.description:
Hackers, possibly using AI-assisted tools, were able to target SAP's (SAP) source code stored on GitHub, according to Der Spiegel, which said the German-based enterprise software firm had confirmed the attack.

Once SAP identified suspicious activity within GitHub, the company immediately took action to mitigate the attack and protect its customers and services, according to the report. The hackers had gained access by acquiring employee authentication tokens, which allowed them to copy and alter source code in GitHub.

"Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," SAP said, according to SecurityWeek.

There was also no evidence of tampered code being delivered to SAP's clients. Some of the protective measures included the replacement of signing keys, limited access to GitHub and a suspension of automated development operations.

Seeking Alpha reached out to SAP for comment.

There has been a clear increase in cyberattacks across businesses, government agencies and critical infrastructure. It was reported on Friday that hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform in a development that could jeopardize sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

data.title: Palantir rises as company signs 5-year, $300M deal with Poland
data.description:
• Palantir (PLTR) shares rose 3% in premarket trading on Friday as the enterprise software giant has signed a five-year deal with Poland worth roughly $300M, the country's defense minister said.
  • The deal will see Palantir provide artificial intelligence-enfused software to help the country's army commanders with their decision-making processes.
  • “We will use (the ​software) to build the best ​possible capabilities. All keys, servers, and information are — ‌and ⁠will remain — the exclusive property of the Polish Armed Forces,” Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said, according to Reuters. Kosiniak-Kamysz added this deal is a “watershed moment” for Poland's armed forces and their capabilities.
  • Earlier this month, Palantir reported third-quarter results that were better-than-expected and upped its full-year guidance, due in part to strong momentum in government contracts.
  • Palantir shares are down 2.5% year-to-date but up more than 670% over the past five years.

data.title: From squishies to can crushers: The toys on the top of Santa's list
data.description:
Forget about an official Red Ryder Carbine-Action 200-shot range model air rifle—the toys kids are waiting to unwrap this holiday season are squishy, loud, and, as always, pricey.

Compiling a list of the most popular toys depends on who you ask. Amazon (AMZN) and Target (TGT) are probably the most popular destinations for kids under 10, while kids 10 and up would most likely prefer their parents shop at Best Buy (BBY) for game consoles, laptops, earbuds, and, of course, the digital download code for Grand Theft Auto VI (TTWO).

Doubling as both collectibles and a calming sensory tool, squishies—including dumpling squishies—are still at the top spot at both Amazon (AMZN) and Target (TGT). The tactile toys are made from slow-rising polyurethane foam that gives a satisfying squeeze and are available in almost unlimited shapes and sizes—from raindrop-shaped squishies to animal-shaped squishies to squishies shaped like a stick of butter.

For creative types, Stickerbox lets kids (and some adults) make their own stickers using AI to generate designs and is equipped with thermal printing that avoids costly ink refills. The $130 Stickerbox is designed to block inappropriate prompts to make sure each sticker is kid-friendly.

Expanding on its "dinosaur hatching" phenomenon from last year, Primal Hatch now allows kids to hatch their own megalodon. Put the egg in the tank, add water, and watch while a shark is “born.” Best part? The color-changing, explosive hatching action can be repeated over and over. Primal Hatch is available at Amazon (AMZN), Walmart (WMT), and Target (TGT) with Amazon (AMZN) offering the best price of $35.

Got a young recycler at home? The Crunchinator and ChompSaw let kids crush empty soda cans and cut up cardboard boxes instead of tossing them.

Designed by a NASA engineer, the $35 Crunchinator enables kids to crush and smash objects in what the company calls “the most satisfyingly destructive ways possible.”

To make use of all those empty Amazon boxes, the $130 Chompshop Chompsaw cuts old cardboard boxes into any shape and any creation to make dioramas, classroom projects, costumes, and whatever else kids can dream up.

For more mindless entertainment, there’s the flying orb ball toy, a “hand-controlled mini drone flight spinner” that can fly, hover, and even respond like a boomerang, all with RGB lighting that creates a mesmerizing light display.

Mattel (MAT) is continuing to cash in on the KPop juggernaut with a new line of KPop Demon Hunters toys, while Disney (DIS) is leaning on a holiday evergreen—a Toy Story figurine line featuring Woody, Jessie, Buzz, Slinky, Rex, and Forky in movie-inspired scale.

Electronics are still a favorite among teens, tweens, and adults with the Consumer Technology Association finding that at least 87% of adults plan to buy tech gifts this holiday season. The most popular for 2026 includes Apple (AAPL) AirPods 5, Sony (SONY) cameras, and Ray-Ban Meta (META) smart glasses, showing that the most-wanted gifts still come with a charging cable.

Target (TGT), Amazon (AMZN), and Best Buy (BBY) all have the Nintendo (NTDOY) Switch 2 Console as one of its bestselling items this holiday season. The next generation of the Nintendo Switch comes with a $500 price tag but gives gamers three play modes: TV, tabletop, and handheld. While the console is compatible with all Nintendo Switch games, it still can’t get you to Vice City.

The toys might change every year—still squishy, still loud, and still pricey—but the mission never does: find the right one before someone else does.

data.title: BofA sets 2027 S&P 500 target at 7,800 after pullback
data.description:
Bank of America Securities this week introduced a 2027 year-end S&P 500 (SP500) target of 7,800, contending that a recent market pullback has created an attractive entry point despite looming earnings deceleration and supply-demand headwinds.

The forecast implies roughly 8.6% upside from Wednesday’s close of 7,182.86—and about 7% from Friday’s implied futures open of 7,290.94—with BofA’s underlying models mapping a wider potential range between 6,600 and 8,500. The index's all-time intraday high is 7,844.52, set in October.

Strategists remain constructive on the back of compressed price-to-earnings multiples and untapped AI-driven productivity gains, noting that higher capital costs and regulatory hurdles should prevent an AI capital expenditure overheat. Reflecting greater value for existing AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) capacity, BofA upgraded communication services (XLC) to Overweight while highlighting stronger conviction in AI adoption through Overweight ratings on financials (XLF) and health care (XLV).

Still, BofA projects S&P 500 earnings-per-share growth to slow sharply from 35% ($370) in 2026 to 14% ($420) in 2027—modestly below the $428 consensus—before normalizing to 7% ($450) in 2028. Because chipmakers (SMH) (SOXX) drive the bulk of profit growth, a 20% cut in AI spending could directly shave 8% off index EPS, compounding broader downside risks from rising equity issuance, waning share buybacks, and potential demographic-driven retirement outflows.
